_meta.description: GPU catalog for the VRAM/throughput planner — capacity, bandwidth, dense BF16 compute, and 3-tier hourly pricing. Keyed by slug (t4-16, a100-80, ...), the same convention benchmarks/data.json's GPU half of each key uses. index.html's GPU_TABLE and generate_report.py's GPUS are generated from this file by tools/sync_data.py, between 'GPU_TABLE:BEGIN'/'GPU_TABLE:END' marker comments in each — edit this file, then re-run that script; do not hand-edit the generated blocks. The row schema carries what both engines read plus the structural fields the v1.1 work needs (vendor, perfKey, devices, form, caps). It is designed to grow — a vendor tag, a per-board device count, a fabric/interconnect tier are all expected to land on this same table in later commits — so a new column is the likely shape of that change, not a new table.

schema.gb: VRAM per card, in GiB. Matches the manufacturer's marketing number, which is already GiB in practice — nvidia-smi reports an '80 GB' H100 as 79.6 GiB, not 80/1e9*2^30 worth of decimal GB.
schema.bw: Memory bandwidth in GB/s, used as the decode roofline's bandwidth term.
schema.hyper: Hyperscaler on-demand price in $/hr per GPU (AWS/GCP/Azure).
schema.spec: Specialized-cloud price in $/hr per GPU (Lambda, CoreWeave, RunPod and similar).
schema.spot: Spot/marketplace price in $/hr per GPU (Vast.ai and similar). Any of hyper/spec/spot may be null — and only those three, which tools/sync_data.py enforces — when no provider's own page confirms an hourly price for the card in that tier: every surface then reads "no confirmed hourly price" with no figure, cost ranges span only the priced tiers, a null tier carries no priceSource but a priceNote saying why, and tools/price_check.py never fetches it (its SOURCE_MAP entry must be manual).
schema.tflops: Dense BF16 tensor-core TFLOPS. NVIDIA datasheets headline the 2:4-structured-sparsity number (e.g. H100 SXM '1,979 teraFLOPS* / *With sparsity'); LLM inference does not use structured sparsity, so this is the dense figure — half the headline number.
schema.name: Display name shown in the GPU dropdown's option label and in generate_report.py's PDF/CLI output, e.g. 'H100 80 GB'.
schema.vendor: The hardware vendor: 'nvidia' or 'amd'. Carried onto each engine's state but read by neither engine's arithmetic: it used to select the PERF constants, and that is perfKey's job now, because one vendor spans architectures whose measured constants differ. Kept for vendor-specific deployment guidance, which is a different question from how fast a card is.
schema.perfKey: Which entry of each engine's PERF table (memory-bandwidth utilisation, decode/prefill MFU, observed band) this card's throughput and TTFT are computed with. 'nvidia' on every NVIDIA row; the AMD rows carry 'cdna2' (MI210, MI250X), 'cdna3' (MI300X, MI325X) and 'rdna3' (RX 7900 XTX), none of which has a PERF entry, because no ROCm utilisation measurements are published to derive one from. Named for a set of measured constants, not for a vendor, so rows share an entry only when the same measurements apply to them. A perfKey with no PERF entry is a supported state, not an error: the card still gets its full VRAM breakdown, fit verdict, cost and vLLM command, while every throughput and TTFT figure is absent (null, never 0) and each view says that no measured utilisation is published for it. Neither engine falls back to another entry's constants. Required on every row — tools/sync_data.py refuses a row without it — so an omission cannot quietly select anything.
schema.devices: How many independent accelerator devices one board presents to the runtime. 1 for every card except the MI250X, which is one OAM containing two GCDs that ROCm enumerates as two GPUs: it is one catalog row with devices:2 and the board's own gb/bw/tflops, because that is how they are bought and priced, and the engine multiplies rather than the catalog duplicating a row.
schema.form: Board form factor: 'sxm', 'oam', 'pcie' or 'consumer'. Read as the NVLink gate — only sxm boards carry it — and as the name of the link a board's devices share: NVLink on an sxm board with it selected, Infinity Fabric on an oam board (AMD's OAM platforms, where that link is part of the platform rather than an option), PCIe otherwise. Both engines derive the name in one place, interconnectName() in index.html and interconnect_name() in generate_report.py; the arithmetic prices Infinity Fabric like any other link that is not NVLink, since nothing here measures it.
schema.caps: Architecture-determined capability flags. caps.fp8 is FP8 matrix support in the silicon: false on Turing (T4) and Ampere (A100), true from Ada and Hopper on; false on AMD's CDNA2 (MI210, MI250X) and RDNA3 (RX 7900 XTX), true on CDNA3 (MI300X, MI325X), per ROCm's precision-support table. Whether vLLM runs an FP8 model on a given card is a separate question.
schema.default: Present and true on exactly one row: the card the tool selects when nothing else is specified. Derived by both engines instead of each hardcoding a slug.
schema.priceSource: Provenance for hyper/spec/spot, written by tools/price_check.py — read by both engines' cost surfaces (index.html's renderCost/renderComparisons/renderExecutiveSummary/exportSummary, generate_report.py's PDF cost section) to name the provider a price came from instead of the three-provider tier description the table used to show for every row. tools/sync_data.py carries it through GPU_OPTIONAL into both generated GPU_TABLE blocks like any other optional field. Optional object keyed by tier name ('hyper'/'spec'/'spot'); a tier key is present only once that tier's price has been confirmed against a live source, as { provider, sku, region, date, price }: provider is the source ('azure'/'aws'/'lambda'/'coreweave'/'vast'), sku is that provider's own SKU/instance-type/meter/plan name (verbatim, e.g. 'Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5'), region is the provider's region ('eastus') or 'global' for sources with no regional pricing, date ('YYYY-MM-DD', UTC) is when it was read, and price is the per-GPU $/hr figure that reading actually compared against the catalog's hyper/spec/spot value, rounded to 2 decimals like every other price here. For a MOVED tier this equals the catalog value by construction; for a CONFIRMED one it can be up to price_check.py's 1% confirm floor away from it, because CONFIRMED refreshes provenance without rewriting a price that moved less than that — tests/price_check.test.py pins that gap. A tier missing from priceSource means no automated provenance is recorded for it: either no automatable source exists for that tier (tools/price_check.py's SOURCE_MAP says which, and why, per slug) or its price is stale and past the tool's flag threshold, held back for a human decision. rtx5090-32 and rtx6000ada-48 carry the field on no tier at all — SOURCE_MAP has no automatable source for either card on any tier. Absence is not an error, and the tool never invents a value to fill it.
schema.priceRecord: A price read by a person off the provider's own page, for a tier no automated source reads — tools/price_check.py's SOURCE_MAP entry for that tier is manual. Optional object keyed by tier name, as { provider, sku, region, date, price, url }: provider is the provider's display name ('RunPod'), sku its own plan or instance name verbatim, region its region or 'global', date ('YYYY-MM-DD') the day it was read, price the per-GPU $/hr that page showed (the catalog value must agree within half a percent, as for priceSource), and url the page itself, so a reader can check it. Both engines show it as '<provider> · <sku> · <region> · recorded by hand <date>, not re-checked weekly'. Never on a tier that has a priceSource, never on a null tier, and nothing re-reads it: it ages until a person reads the page again. tests/price_check.test.py holds every record to these rules.
schema.priceNote: Why a price tier has neither a priceSource nor a priceRecord. Optional object keyed by tier name, as { reason, checked }: reason says where the tier's figure came from and why no weekly reader covers it, or, on a null tier, why no hourly price qualified — in sentences, and never with a dollar figure, since a figure beside the tier's own would read as a price; checked ('YYYY-MM-DD') is the day the reason was last verified. Every tier of every row carries exactly one of priceSource, priceRecord and priceNote, which tests/price_check.test.py enforces, so no tier shows a figure, or its absence, without saying how it got there. Both engines show it under the tier's label as '<reason> Checked <checked>.' in the cost table, the copied report and the PDF. tools/price_check.py --apply removes a tier's note when it records a priceSource for that tier.
schema.priceLead: An hourly price found for a tier that has no confirmed price, and not used: optional object keyed by tier name, each a list of { provider, price, url, date, why, about? }. provider is the display name, price the per-GPU $/hr the page showed, url the page it was read on, date ('YYYY-MM-DD') the day it was read, why a sentence saying why it could not be confirmed, and about an optional link to what is known about the provider. Only on a null tier, which tests/price_check.test.py enforces. Both engines show it under the tier's note as 'Lead, not used: <provider> lists $<price>/hr (read <date>)' with why and its links, in the cost table, the copied report and the PDF, and no figure anywhere reads it: a lead can be removed without changing any number the tool prints. The first leads are Runcrate's (owner decision 2026-09-23, docs/research/runcrate-due-diligence.md).
